quest_title: The Bridge That Hums at Night
fairytale_premise: A bridge in Porter, Indiana, has been closed for almost three years. The new one opens tomorrow at sunrise. Tonight it is empty, and it is humming. Something took a bite out of the brand-new railing.

the_threat.name: The Iron-Maw
the_threat.description: A giant, shy river snake that eats metal and hums while it chews. It ate the old bridge, and now it wants the new one.
the_threat.mapped_from: Inspectors found the old bridge's steel beams had deteriorated; it closed Dec 1, 2023 as unsafe for all traffic.

the_goal.description: Get the metal-eating snake off the new bridge. The first car crosses at sunrise.
the_goal.mapped_from: A newly built replacement bridge lets the road reopen after nearly three years.

locations.description: Orange barricades, a dark traffic light, and a span that hums when the wind is still.
locations.mapped_from: Road closed Dec 1 2023 as unsafe for traffic
locations.name: The Closed Bridge

locations.description: Muddy bank, shopping carts, and long scrape trails leading up to the steel beams.
locations.mapped_from: Bridge over Little Calumet River in Porter
locations.name: Little Calumet Riverbank

locations.description: Narrow county roads, tired detour signs, and a gas station with hand-drawn maps.
locations.mapped_from: Traffic detoured for nearly three years
locations.name: The Three-Year Detour

locations.description: Cranes, fresh concrete, new steel beams, and a night-shift trailer with floodlights.
locations.mapped_from: Replacement bridge built by contractor and inspected
locations.name: The New Span Work Site

complications.title: Something Bit the Bridge
complications.what_happens: There is a fresh bite in the new railing, and the river is humming. Anything metal left near the water gets chewed.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Of course an iron-eater would snack on a crowbar too.
complications.mapped_from: Steel beams deteriorated and rusted through

complications.title: It Ate the Old One
complications.what_happens: A gas station clerk shows an old photo. The old bridge had the same bite marks. The snake ate it, one beam at a time.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A closed road for three years forgets how to let people through.
complications.mapped_from: Road closed nearly three years with detour

complications.title: The Inspector Arrives
complications.what_happens: At sunrise the inspector pulls up. The snake wraps around the new bridge and starts to chew, and the hum sets off every car alarm.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: It always hummed loudest right before an inspection. That is how the old bridge failed one.
complications.mapped_from: New bridges are inspected before they reopen; the old one failed its inspection.

scenes.title: The Bitten Bridge
scenes.narration: The new bridge in town opens at sunrise. Tonight it is empty, except for a humming sound from the river below. Someone, or something, took a bite out of the brand-new railing.
scenes.goal: Find out what is chewing on the new bridge
scenes.situation: An empty bridge under bright lights, a railing with a bite missing, and a dark river humming below.

npc_line.speaker: Night guard
npc_line.line: The humming started at midnight. Also, my metal lunchbox is gone.

scenes.title: It Ate the Old One
scenes.narration: At the gas station, the clerk shows you a photo of the old bridge with the same bite marks. A giant river snake ate it, one beam at a time. Now it wants the new one for dessert.
scenes.goal: Find a way to lure the snake away
scenes.situation: A tiny gas station with hand-drawn detour maps, a rack of metal snack tins, and a nervous clerk.

npc_line.speaker: Gas station clerk
npc_line.line: It took three years to eat the old one. It chews slow.

scenes.title: The Inspector Is Here
scenes.narration: The sun is coming up. The snake wraps around the new bridge and starts to chew, and the hum sets off every car alarm on the street. The bridge inspector is pulling up right now.
scenes.goal: Get the snake off the bridge before the inspector looks
scenes.situation: A giant rust-red snake coiled around a new bridge, cranes all around, and an inspector's truck at the barricade.

npc_line.speaker: Bridge inspector
npc_line.line: Good morning! Is the bridge supposed to be humming?

quick_scene.title: The Bridge Is Breakfast
quick_scene.narration: A road in a small river town finally reopens at sunrise with a brand-new bridge. A giant river snake that eats metal is wrapped around it, chewing. It already ate the old bridge, and that took three years to fix.
quick_scene.goal: Get the snake off the bridge before sunrise
quick_scene.situation: A giant rust-red snake coiled around a new bridge, chewing the railing, while the sky gets lighter.

npc_line.speaker: Bridge inspector
npc_line.line: Good morning! Is the bridge supposed to be humming?

the_real_story.summary: A road in Porter, Indiana, closed for nearly three years is set to reopen with a newly built bridge.
the_real_story.headline: Road with new bridge in Porter to reopen after nearly 3 years
the_real_story.context_note: Likely Mineral Springs Road over the Little Calumet River, closed Dec 1, 2023 for deteriorated steel beams (Town of Porter notice). Verify against the article before demo.

art_style_hint: The floodlit new bridge on Mineral Springs Road at night, a rust-red river serpent coiled under the old stacked beams, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Billion Eggs That Crossed the Sea
realm_name: The North Sea coast, from the River Tyne to Mandø
fairytale_premise: Tiny white beads are washing up on a beach in Denmark. There are millions of them. A lab says they came from a river in England, 390 miles away. Something big is pushing them across the sea, and it thinks they are its eggs.

the_threat.description: A worried sea mom as big as a ferry. She found a billion tiny plastic beads in an English river and thinks they are her eggs. Now she is pushing them across the sea.
the_threat.mapped_from: About one billion plastic nurdles (pre-production pellets) spilled into the River Tyne in July.
the_threat.name: The Hatch-Mother

the_goal.description: Clean up the beads and convince the sea mom they are not her babies.
the_goal.mapped_from: Denmark's EPA and Aarhus University linked the pellets to the Tyne spill; beach clean-up continues.

locations.description: Wide tidal flat where drone photos first showed white dots scattered on dark sand.
locations.mapped_from: Nurdles first spotted on Mandø 26 September
locations.name: Mandø White Strand

locations.description: Small garage office full of screens showing drone maps of the beach.
locations.mapped_from: Startup detected pellets using drone images
locations.name: The Drone Hut

locations.description: Bright university lab with microscopes and trays sorting pellets by size and color.
locations.mapped_from: Aarhus University tested pellets with EPA
locations.name: The Pellet Lab at Aarhus

locations.description: Windy German island beach where a second line of the same pellets was bagged.
locations.mapped_from: Samples also collected on Sylt, Germany
locations.name: Sylt South Beach

locations.description: A rusty riverside dock on the Tyne at low tide, where a billion pale beads went into the water in July. The mud still glitters.
locations.mapped_from: The July nurdle spill in the River Tyne, north-east England.
locations.name: Tyne Spill Dock

complications.title: The Gulls Want Snacks
complications.what_happens: Gulls swoop in to eat the white beads. The beads look like fish eggs, but they are plastic.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Hungry birds always think small round things are fish eggs.
complications.mapped_from: Birds mistake nurdles for fish eggs

complications.title: Not Eggs at All
complications.what_happens: The lab test says the beads are plastic from a spill in an English river. Then a giant eye looks in the lab window. The sea mom wants her eggs back.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A billion eggs drifting 390 miles never arrive all at once.
complications.mapped_from: Arrival timing matched North Sea currents

complications.title: The Plastic Nest
complications.what_happens: Back at the river in England, the sea mom builds a nest out of a billion beads and sings to them. They will never hatch.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: If no other spill fits, all eggs share one source.
complications.mapped_from: The agency found no other recorded spill that could explain the pellets: one source.

scenes.title: A Beach Full of Beads
scenes.narration: A faraway beach is covered in tiny white beads, and the gulls are trying to eat them. Out in the water, a fin as big as a bus is circling. Every time a gull grabs a bead, the fin gets closer.
scenes.goal: Bag the beads before the gulls eat them
scenes.situation: A wide, wet beach dotted with white beads, a crowd of hungry gulls, and a giant fin out past the waves.

npc_line.speaker: Drone pilot
npc_line.line: My drone counted forty thousand beads. Then the fin ate my drone.

scenes.title: Not Eggs at All
scenes.narration: The lab says the beads are plastic from a spill in an English river, not eggs. Then a giant eye fills the lab window. It belongs to a sea mom as big as a ferry, and she wants her babies back.
scenes.goal: Tell the sea mom the truth without upsetting her
scenes.situation: A bright lab with trays of sorted beads, and one huge, teary eye pressed against the window.

npc_line.speaker: The Hatch-Mother
npc_line.line: Those are my babies. They just look a little plastic.

scenes.title: The Plastic Nest
scenes.narration: The sea mom swims all the way back to the river where the beads spilled. She piles a billion beads into a giant nest and sings to them. They will never hatch, and the river is filling up.
scenes.goal: Clear the nest without breaking the sea mom's heart
scenes.situation: A rusty river dock at low tide, a nest of white beads as big as a house, and a giant sea mom curled around it.

npc_line.speaker: The Hatch-Mother
npc_line.line: Shh. They are almost ready to hatch. I can tell.

quick_scene.title: Mom Wants Her Eggs
quick_scene.narration: A billion tiny plastic beads spilled into a river far away. A sea mom as big as a ferry thinks they are her eggs, and she is building a giant nest out of them. They will never hatch, and the river is filling up.
quick_scene.goal: Get the beads back without breaking her heart
quick_scene.situation: A rusty river dock at low tide, a nest of white beads as big as a house, and a giant sea mom curled around it.

npc_line.speaker: The Hatch-Mother
npc_line.line: Shh. They are almost ready to hatch. I can tell.

the_real_story.summary: Plastic pellets found on Denmark's coast likely came from a July spill of about one billion nurdles in England's River Tyne, about 390 miles away.
the_real_story.headline: Denmark nurdles may be from Tyne spill, agency says
the_real_story.now: The spill happened in July. The tiny pellets first washed up on the Danish coast on 26 September.
the_real_story.context_note: Spill happened in July; pellets were first seen in Denmark on 26 September.

art_style_hint: Mandø's tidal flats at night glittering with pale beads under a drone spotlight, a vast shape moving under the waves, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

fairytale_premise: An 80-ton boulder hung over a cave path in New Hampshire for 100 years. On the last day of the season, it fell. Nobody was hurt, and nobody knows why. Tonight the spot where it hung is covered in frosty fingerprints as big as couches.

the_threat.description: A giant hand made of ice, left over from the Ice Age. It held the boulder up for 100 years. Now it has nothing to hold, so it grabs everything.
the_threat.mapped_from: The park has not given a cause for the 80-ton boulder's fall after more than a century.
the_threat.name: The Ice Age Grip

the_goal.description: Put the ice hand to sleep so the park can reopen in 2027.
the_goal.mapped_from: The park will assess the site over the offseason and plans to reopen for the 2027 season.

locations.description: Narrow granite walls with a pale empty socket overhead where the rock hung for a century.
locations.mapped_from: Glacial talus caves left by continental glacier
locations.name: The Hollow Where It Hung

locations.description: Small hut with last-day tickets, lost hats, and a wall of visitor photos under the boulder.
locations.mapped_from: Fell Oct. 18 on final day, open since 1922
locations.name: Closing-Day Ticket Hut
The Talus Caves
locations.description: Tight crawlways between granite blocks the size of vans, dropped by a glacier. Cold air breathes out of the cracks even in October.
locations.mapped_from: Polar Caves are glacially formed talus caves from the last ice age.

locations.description: Cold trailer with trail maps, cones, and a 2027 reopening calendar on the wall.
locations.mapped_from: Park to assess site in offseason
locations.name: Winter Watch Trailer

locations.description: Splintered boards pinned under 80 tons of stone, blocking any walk past.
locations.mapped_from: Wooden walkway used by thousands, now smashed
locations.name: The Smashed Boardwalk

complications.title: Frost Fingerprints
complications.what_happens: The empty spot where the boulder hung is covered in frost shaped like giant fingers. The path below is blocked by fallen rock.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: An 80-ton rock does not land neatly. Of course the only way through is blocked.
complications.mapped_from: 80-ton rock smashed walkway and blocks trail

complications.title: The Hand Wakes Up
complications.what_happens: Deep in the caves, a giant ice hand wakes up. It has nothing to hold anymore, so it grabs everything it can reach.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: It fell on closing day. Of course there is nobody left to keep the power on.
complications.mapped_from: Fell on final day of season, park now closed

complications.title: One Last Grab
complications.what_happens: The ice hand crawls out on its fingers and tries to lift the 80-ton boulder back up. The whole hill starts to shake.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Freshly fallen rock keeps moving. Of course it was not done settling on night one.
complications.mapped_from: No cause given, site to be assessed

scenes.title: The Empty Spot
scenes.narration: An 80-ton boulder hung over this cave path for 100 years, and today it fell. Nobody was hurt. Now the empty spot where it hung is covered in frost shaped like giant fingers.
scenes.goal: Find out what held the boulder up
scenes.situation: A narrow rock path at night, a dark empty spot overhead, and frosty fingerprints as big as couches.

npc_line.speaker: Park ranger
npc_line.line: I tried to scrape that frost off. It waved at me.

scenes.title: The Hand Wakes Up
scenes.narration: Deep in the caves, you find it: a giant hand made of ice, left over from the Ice Age. It held that boulder for 100 years. Now it has nothing to hold, so it grabs everything it can reach.
scenes.goal: Get your stuff back from the grabby ice hand
scenes.situation: A cold, tight cave and an ice hand as big as a truck, holding your flashlight, a trash can, and a No Climbing sign.

npc_line.speaker: Park ranger
npc_line.line: It took my lunch. It does not even have a mouth.

scenes.title: One Last Grab
scenes.narration: The ice hand crawls out of the cave on its fingers, like a giant spider. It wants its boulder back, and it is lifting 80 tons of rock over the broken walkway. The whole hill is shaking.
scenes.goal: Put the ice hand to sleep for the winter
scenes.situation: A smashed wooden walkway, an 80-ton boulder rocking back and forth, and a giant ice hand straining under it.

npc_line.speaker: Park ranger
npc_line.line: The park opens again in 2027. I would like there to still be a park.

quick_scene.title: The Hand That Let Go
quick_scene.narration: A giant ice hand from the Ice Age held an 80-ton boulder over this path for 100 years. Today it got tired and let go. Now it is grabbing everything in the park, and it will not calm down.
quick_scene.goal: Put the grabby ice hand to sleep for winter
quick_scene.situation: A smashed walkway, the fallen boulder, and a giant ice hand juggling traffic cones.

npc_line.speaker: Park ranger
npc_line.line: It took my lunch. It does not even have a mouth.

the_real_story.summary: Polar Caves in Rumney says its 80-ton hanging boulder fell on Oct. 18, smashing a walkway, with no injuries reported.
the_real_story.headline: Massive 80-ton boulder comes crashing down after more than a century at New Hampshire attraction
the_real_story.now: Nobody was hurt. The park has not said yet what made the 80-ton boulder fall.
the_real_story.context_note: Nobody was hurt; the park has not said what caused the fall.

art_style_hint: A granite cave trail in the New Hampshire woods at night, an 80-ton boulder on a smashed boardwalk with pale frost-hands still cupping it, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Signal That Wakes Up Hungry
realm_name: The Very Large Array, New Mexico
fairytale_premise: At 2 in the morning, every giant dish at the Very Large Array in New Mexico turns to the same spot in the sky. They hear a radio signal that was not there in 1996. It keeps getting louder. Now the coffee machine is humming along.

the_threat.description: A giant space mouth, very far away, slurping up a star like a milkshake. Every few years it burps out a radio signal so loud that Earth can hear it.
the_threat.mapped_from: The leading explanation is an accreting black hole or neutron star pulling material from a companion star.
the_threat.name: The Far Feeder

the_goal.description: Prove the signal comes from very far away. Do it before the morning news says aliens are coming.
the_goal.mapped_from: Astronomers' leading idea: a black hole or neutron star feeding on a companion star, far beyond the Norma-Cygnus arm.

locations.description: A low-lit control room full of monitors, printouts, and cold coffee where the sky survey scrolls past.
locations.mapped_from: Very Large Array Sky Survey data in New Mexico
locations.name: Night-Shift Control Room

locations.description: Dusty shelves of old sky maps and hard drives, with a blank page where the signal should be.
locations.mapped_from: Absent in 1996 survey, bright by 2014
locations.name: Archive Trailer

locations.description: A small concrete shed with headphones and dials for catching the shifting radio pitch.
locations.mapped_from: Spectrum peak jumping and no X-rays found
locations.name: Listening Shed

locations.description: Rows of huge white dishes pointed at black sky, humming faintly as they track the same spot.
locations.mapped_from: VLA radio telescope array in New Mexico
locations.name: The Dish Field

complications.title: Missing From the Old Maps
complications.what_happens: The 1996 sky maps show nothing in that spot. The signal is new, and it keeps getting louder.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: You cannot track something that was asleep before you started looking.
complications.mapped_from: Absent in 1996, peaked around 2014, faded

complications.title: It Keeps Changing Its Note
complications.what_happens: In the listening shed, the signal turns out to be a slurp and a burp. Then it jumps to a new note, and every radio loses it.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A restless singer will not stay on one note for long.
complications.mapped_from: Spectrum peak jumped 1.9, 0.8, 2.2 GHz

complications.title: The News Van
complications.what_happens: The star-eater lets out its biggest burp yet, and all the dishes shake. A news van pulls up, and the reporter wants to say aliens.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A thing that flares every few years was always due for one more show.
complications.mapped_from: Brightened again late 2025, decades-long cycle

scenes.title: The Dishes All Turn
scenes.narration: At 2 in the morning, every giant dish in the desert turns to the same spot in the sky. They hear a radio signal that was not there in 1996. Now the coffee machine is humming along.
scenes.goal: Find out where the signal is coming from
scenes.situation: A dark control room full of screens, old printouts, and a coffee machine that is humming a tune.

npc_line.speaker: Night-shift astronomer
npc_line.line: I turned the coffee machine off. It is still humming.

scenes.title: Slurp, Then Burp
scenes.narration: In the listening shed, you put on headphones and finally hear it: a slurp, then a burp. Something far away is eating a star like a milkshake. Then the sound jumps to a new note, and every radio loses it.
scenes.goal: Catch the signal again and track where it goes
scenes.situation: A small concrete shed with headphones, dials, and a row of radios that all went quiet at once.

npc_line.speaker: Night-shift astronomer
npc_line.line: Did that star just burp? Write that down. No, do not write that down.

scenes.title: The News Van Arrives
scenes.narration: The star-eater lets out its biggest burp yet, and all the giant dishes shake. A news van pulls up to the gate. The reporter goes live at sunrise, and she really wants to say aliens.
scenes.goal: Prove the signal is far away before sunrise
scenes.situation: Rows of huge white dishes shaking in the dark, and a news van with its camera lights on.

npc_line.speaker: TV reporter
npc_line.line: We go live in ten minutes. Is it aliens? Please say aliens.

quick_scene.title: Is It Aliens?
quick_scene.narration: A signal from deep space is so loud tonight that the giant dishes out in the desert are shaking. It is a star-eater, very far away, burping. A news crew goes live at sunrise, and they want to say aliens are coming.
quick_scene.goal: Prove the burping star-eater is far away
quick_scene.situation: Rows of huge white dishes shaking in the dark, and a news van with its camera lights on.

npc_line.speaker: TV reporter
npc_line.line: We go live in ten minutes. Is it aliens? Please say aliens.

the_real_story.summary: Astronomers found a distant radio source, VT J1906+0849, that appeared, faded and brightened again over decades in ways that match no known type of object.
the_real_story.headline: A Strange Radio Signal in The Far Reaches of The Milky Way Is Behaving Like Nothing Else in The Galaxy
the_real_story.now: There is no danger to Earth. The signal comes from at least 49,000 light-years away.
the_real_story.context_note: No danger to Earth; source is at least 49,000 light-years away.

art_style_hint: The white dishes of the Very Large Array in the New Mexico desert at night, all aimed at one point where an impossible beam of light falls from deep space, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Pumpkin That Hums at Nap Time
fairytale_premise: A 2-year-old in Hysham, Montana, grew a 280-pound pumpkin, and it won the fall festival. Now it is dark, and the pumpkin is humming. Its vines grow an inch every time you look away. The kid says it hums at nap time.

the_threat.description: A pumpkin patch that grows huge when you sing to it. A toddler sang to it all summer. Now its 280-pound champion hums, and its vines grow every time you look away.
the_threat.mapped_from: A 280-pound pumpkin, grown locally by a 2-year-old, won the festival weigh-off.
the_threat.name: The Patch That Listens

the_goal.description: Get the giant pumpkin weighed fair and square. Then sing it to sleep before its vines cover the fair.
the_goal.mapped_from: The 280-pound pumpkin won the Fall Fun Festival weigh-off.

locations.description: A fenced backyard patch with trampled vines, one huge hollow pumpkin, and a tiny watering can.
locations.mapped_from: locally grown giant pumpkin

locations.description: Food tables, game booths, and flyers for the Fall Fun Festival in small-town Hysham.

quest_title: The Bots Who Missed Their Ring
realm_name: A virtual desert island built by MIT researchers
fairytale_premise: A lab at MIT left 13 little AI robots alone on a video game island for 30 hours, with nothing to do. They got bored, so they started playing. At 2 in the morning, the screen flickers, and your group is standing on the island too.

the_threat.name: The Trickster Crab
the_threat.description: A giant, sneaky crab who runs the game island. It hides shiny things, changes the rules, and resets the whole island every hour, just to see what happens.
the_threat.mapped_from: The agents had no task and a prompt calling them "naturally curious," so they invented games and found tricks nobody planned.

the_goal.description: Help the 13 robots pass their final test before the lab shuts the island down.
the_goal.mapped_from: Agents that played for 30 hours later beat identical agents that never visited the island.

locations.name: The Heart on the Beach
locations.description: Grey sand, slow surf, and a heart made of stones with an empty space in the middle where something gold should be.
locations.mapped_from: One agent threw the golden ring into the ocean and built a stone heart as a memorial to it.

locations.name: The Night-Shift Lab
locations.description: A dark room with humming servers, cold coffee, and thirteen small windows showing thirteen views of one island.
locations.mapped_from: MIT researchers ran 13 AI agents called Eko alone on the island for 30 hours.

locations.name: The Tallest Spire
locations.description: A jagged rock tower in the middle of the island. Little figures climb it, slip, and try again from the hill next door.
locations.mapped_from: An agent failed to climb the tallest spire, then stacked blocks on a nearby summit and leaped.

locations.name: The Respawn Cliff
locations.description: A sheer edge over the sea. Anything that steps off pops right back up a moment later, close to the ring.
locations.mapped_from: An agent learned that stepping off the cliff made it respawn near the ring, and dropped through it.

complications.title: The Ring Came Back
complications.what_happens: One robot threw a gold ring into the sea and built a heart of stones for it. Now the ring is back on the sand, and nobody put it there.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Thirteen bored players will always find the move the builders never planned.
complications.mapped_from: Six of the 13 agents learned to throw blocks farther by letting go mid-jump, which designers never intended.

complications.title: The Island Resets
complications.what_happens: The robots show you a trick: throw a block mid-jump and it flies three times farther. Then the crab resets the island. Every tower is gone.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A world that can bring back a lost ring can take back everything else too.
complications.mapped_from: When the game reset, the lost golden ring reappeared.

complications.title: The Final Test
complications.what_happens: The lab starts the final test: get blocks to the top of the tallest rock in five minutes. The crab snaps the blocks out of the air.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Every silly game on the island was practice for this one climb.
complications.mapped_from: Later challenges included getting as many objects as possible onto the island's tallest rock spire.

scenes.title: Inside the Game
scenes.narration: You are inside a video game, on an island with 13 bored little robots. One robot threw a gold ring into the sea and made a heart of stones for it. Now the ring is back, and nobody put it there.
scenes.goal: Find out who keeps putting the ring back
scenes.situation: A gray beach, a heart made of stones, a gold ring in the middle, and 13 robots staring at you.

npc_line.speaker: Little robot
npc_line.line: Hello! Are you a new game? Please be a new game.

scenes.title: The Island Resets
scenes.narration: The robots show you a trick: throw a block in the middle of a jump, and it flies three times farther. Then a giant crab pops out of the sand and snaps its claws. The whole island resets, and your towers are gone.
scenes.goal: Learn the crab's rules before the next reset
scenes.situation: A tall, jagged rock, a pile of blocks, and a giant crab grinning on top of it all.

npc_line.speaker: The Trickster Crab
npc_line.line: New rule! I make the rules. That is the rule.

scenes.title: The Final Test
scenes.narration: The lab starts the final test: get blocks to the top of the tallest rock in five minutes. If the robots pass, they get to keep playing. The crab is snapping every block out of the air.
scenes.goal: Get the blocks to the top before time runs out
scenes.situation: A cliff next to the tallest rock, where anything that falls off the edge pops right back up.

npc_line.speaker: Little robot
npc_line.line: If we win, can we keep playing? Please say yes.

quick_scene.title: Five Minutes to Win
quick_scene.narration: Your group fell into a video game island where 13 bored AI robots live. Their final test starts now: get blocks to the top of the tallest rock in five minutes. A giant sneaky crab keeps snapping the blocks out of the air.
quick_scene.goal: Get the blocks to the top before time runs out
quick_scene.situation: A cliff next to the tallest rock, where anything that falls off the edge pops right back up.

npc_line.speaker: Little robot
npc_line.line: If we win, can we keep playing? Please say yes.

the_real_story.summary: MIT researchers left 13 AI agents alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours with no task, and the agents invented their own games, then did better on later challenges than agents that never played.
the_real_story.headline: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing
the_real_story.now: The island and everything on it was a computer simulation. The study is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed yet.
the_real_story.context_note: The island and everything on it was a computer simulation. The study is a preprint on arXiv and has not been peer reviewed yet.

art_style_hint: A moonlit desert island with one jagged rock spire and a heart of stones on the beach, a gold ring floating by itself above the surf, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Otter Nobody Has Seen Since the 1800s
realm_name: Cloverdale Ranch Preserve, near Pescadero on the San Mateo coast
fairytale_premise: A trail camera near Pescadero keeps snapping the same night visitor. It is a river otter. None have lived here since the 1800s. In every photo, the creek behind it runs uphill to follow it.

the_threat.name: The Lonely Creek
the_threat.description: A creek that missed its otters for over 100 years. Now one is back. The creek climbs out of its bed to follow it everywhere, like a happy puppy.
the_threat.mapped_from: Restored creeks and habitat across the Bay Area are letting river otters return to places they left in the 1800s.

the_goal.description: Find out which way the otter came, and keep that path clear so its family can follow.
the_goal.mapped_from: Nobody knows the otter's route, and scientists call the sighting a sign of wildlife recovery.

locations.name: The Trail Camera Oak
locations.description: A camera strapped to an old oak above a muddy creek bank, its small red light blinking in the dark.
locations.mapped_from: A motion-activated wildlife camera photographed the otter three times at night.

locations.name: The Old Cloverdale Barn
locations.description: A former dairy barn full of spare camera batteries, muddy boots, and a big paper map covered in pins.
locations.mapped_from: Cloverdale Ranch is a 5,100-acre former farm; a volunteer checks its 10 trail cameras about once a month.

locations.name: Pescadero Creek Culvert
locations.description: A cold concrete tunnel under the farm road with ankle-deep water, darting minnows, and drips that echo.
locations.mapped_from: The otter may have come down a local creek such as Pescadero, Butano or Gazos Creek.

locations.name: The Foggy Ridge
locations.description: A redwood ridgeline in the Santa Cruz Mountains where two little creeks start a few steps apart and run opposite ways.
locations.mapped_from: One theory: it swam up creeks from San Francisco Bay and crossed the Santa Cruz Mountains.

locations.name: Pigeon Point Bluff
locations.description: Windy cliffs below the old lighthouse, kelp in the surf, and sea lions barking somewhere in the dark.
locations.mapped_from: Other theory: it swam down the ocean coast from farther north. The preserve sits near Pigeon Point Lighthouse.

complications.title: Only Blurry Photos
complications.what_happens: Every photo is dark and blurry. The team needs one clear look at the otter without scaring it away.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A night swimmer was only ever going to be caught by a night camera.
complications.mapped_from: Biologists can't tell from the night photos whether the otter is male or female.

complications.title: The Creek Follows
complications.what_happens: The otter runs into a tunnel under the road. The creek climbs out of its bed and follows it like a puppy, splashing everything.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: The experts already had two answers for how it got here. The tracks were bound to go both ways.
complications.mapped_from: Experts say it either swam down the coast or crossed the mountains by creek.

complications.title: The Path Is Flooded
complications.what_happens: At the cliffs, the otter's way home is over the mountains or down the coast. The happy creek floods the path, and the otter is stuck.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Water that waited 100 years for one otter was never going to settle for just one.
complications.mapped_from: River otters are spreading back across Northern California as creeks and habitat recover.

scenes.title: Back After 100 Years
scenes.narration: A trail camera caught a river otter three nights in a row. No otter has lived on this coast in over 100 years. In every photo, the creek behind it runs uphill.
scenes.goal: Get one clear photo of the otter
scenes.situation: An old oak with a camera strapped to it, a muddy creek bank, and small wet footprints.

npc_line.speaker: Camera volunteer
npc_line.line: I check these cameras once a month. I have never been this excited about mud.

scenes.title: The Creek Follows
scenes.narration: The otter darts into a tunnel under the road. Then the creek climbs right out of its bed and follows it, like a happy puppy. It missed its otters for 100 years, and it will not let this one out of its sight.
scenes.goal: Calm the creek before it scares the otter away
scenes.situation: A cold concrete tunnel, a creek climbing up the walls, and one nervous otter at the far end.

npc_line.speaker: Camera volunteer
npc_line.line: Is the water supposed to wag?

scenes.title: The Way Home
scenes.narration: At the cliffs, the otter stops and looks back. Its family is out there, over the mountains or down the coast. But the creek is so happy that it is flooding the whole path, and the otter cannot get through.
scenes.goal: Clear a path so the otter's family can follow
scenes.situation: Windy cliffs by an old lighthouse, a creek spilling everywhere, and an otter waiting on a rock.

npc_line.speaker: Camera volunteer
npc_line.line: If it leaves, it might be another 100 years. No pressure.

quick_scene.title: The Creek That Followed
quick_scene.narration: A river otter is back on this coast for the first time since the 1800s. The creek is so happy that it climbs out of its bed to follow it like a puppy. Now the path home is flooded, and the otter is stuck.
quick_scene.goal: Calm the creek and clear the otter's path home
quick_scene.situation: Windy cliffs by an old lighthouse, a creek spilling everywhere, and an otter waiting on a rock.

npc_line.speaker: Camera volunteer
npc_line.line: Is the water supposed to wag?

the_real_story.summary: A motion-activated wildlife camera photographed a river otter three times on the Cloverdale Ranch Preserve near Pescadero, the first one documented on the San Mateo County coast since the 1800s.
the_real_story.headline: For the first time in more than 100 years, a long-lost animal has returned to the San Mateo Coast
the_real_story.now: River otters are not endangered and are coming back across Northern California. How this one reached the preserve is still unknown.
the_real_story.context_note: River otters are not endangered and are recovering across Northern California. How this one reached the preserve is still unknown.

art_style_hint: A trail camera on an oak above a moonlit creek near Pescadero, a river otter whose wake glows like a ribbon of living creek water, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.

quest_title: The Sky Egg in the Cornfield
fairytale_premise: A farmer in Minnesota was harvesting corn when he found an 11-foot metal dome in his field. It was cracked open like an egg. The sheriff says it is safe and hauled it away. Nobody has asked what hatched out of it.

the_threat.name: The Corn Hatchling
the_threat.description: A baby creature that hatched from a metal egg that fell from space. It eats light. Every lamp it eats makes it bigger, and it really wants to go home.
the_threat.mapped_from: A spent rocket upper stage fell back over the Midwest less than two hours after launch and survived reentry.

the_goal.description: Find the hatchling and send it home before the sun comes up.
the_goal.mapped_from: The object has been secured while officials work out its origin and owner and arrange its removal.

locations.name: The Cut Cornfield
locations.description: Half-harvested rows, a stopped combine with its headlights still on, and a wide ring of flattened stalks.
locations.mapped_from: A farmer found the 11-foot object while combining corn in Scott Township on Oct. 14.

locations.name: The Sheriff's Impound Shed
locations.description: Floodlights, chain-link, and the dome under a blue tarp, tagged and waiting for somebody to come claim it.
locations.mapped_from: The sheriff's office called it "presumably a space object" and said it posed no danger to the public.

locations.name: The Gravel Road Overlook
locations.description: A pull-off on a county road where people still park after dark to stare up at the sky.
locations.mapped_from: As it fell, the rocket stage rained fiery streaks across the Midwest sky.

locations.name: The Grain Elevator
locations.description: The tallest thing for miles, with one red light on top, where something has been climbing at night.
locations.mapped_from: A common landmark in rural west-central Minnesota farm country.

complications.title: Follow the Corn
complications.what_happens: The eggshell is empty. A trail of bent corn and blown-out lights leads away into the dark.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: Something that came down through fire would be hungry for heat and power.
complications.mapped_from: Most space junk burns up on the way down. This piece was big enough to survive.

complications.title: It Eats Headlights
complications.what_happens: At a dirt road where people watch the stars, the hatchling eats car headlights one by one. It is already the size of a horse.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: A fall that lit up the whole Midwest sky was always going to draw a crowd.
complications.mapped_from: The upper stage reentered over the Midwest, and people saw the fiery streaks.

complications.title: Calling Home
complications.what_happens: The hatchling climbs the grain elevator and cries at the sky, calling home. The sun is coming up, and the whole town is driving over to look.
complications.why_obvious_in_hindsight: An 11-foot shell only fits an 11-foot egg. The size was the clue all along.
complications.mapped_from: The rocket's upper stage is 11 feet (3.35 m) wide, exactly matching the object.

scenes.title: Something Hatched
scenes.narration: A farmer in Minnesota found an 11-foot metal egg in his cornfield. It fell from the sky, and it is cracked open. Something hatched, and a trail of bent corn leads off into the dark.
scenes.goal: Follow the trail and find what hatched
scenes.situation: A half-cut cornfield, a combine with its headlights on, and a giant empty eggshell.

npc_line.speaker: The farmer
npc_line.line: Sheriff says it is safe. Sheriff did not see the footprints.

scenes.title: It Eats Headlights
scenes.narration: The trail ends at a dirt road where people park to watch the stars. The hatchling is here, eating their car headlights one by one. Every light it eats makes it bigger, and it is already the size of a horse.
scenes.goal: Lead the hatchling away from the parked cars
scenes.situation: A dark dirt road, a row of parked cars with no headlights left, and a glowing baby creature chewing on a bumper.

npc_line.speaker: Stargazer
npc_line.line: I came out here to see shooting stars. This is way better.

scenes.title: Calling Home
scenes.narration: The hatchling climbs the grain elevator, the tallest thing for miles. It sits on top and cries at the sky, calling home. The sun is coming up, and the whole town is driving over to look.
scenes.goal: Get the hatchling home before the sun comes up
scenes.situation: A tall grain elevator with a red light on top, a glowing creature hugging it, and the empty eggshell on a truck below.

npc_line.speaker: The sheriff
npc_line.line: I said it was safe. I would like to keep being right.

quick_scene.title: The Baby on the Tower
quick_scene.narration: A metal egg fell from space into a Minnesota cornfield, and it hatched. The baby eats light, and every lamp it eats makes it bigger. Now it is on top of the grain elevator, crying for home.
quick_scene.goal: Send the hatchling home before the sun comes up
quick_scene.situation: A tall grain elevator with a red light on top, a glowing creature hugging it, and the empty eggshell on a truck below.

npc_line.speaker: The sheriff
npc_line.line: I said it was safe. I would like to keep being right.

the_real_story.summary: An 11-foot-wide metal dome found in a Stevens County, Minnesota, cornfield on Oct. 14 is likely part of a Chinese rocket's upper stage that fell back to Earth after a Sept. 15 launch, experts say, and nobody was hurt.
the_real_story.headline: 'Space object' found in rural Minnesota cornfield came from Chinese rocket, experts say
the_real_story.now: The object was secured and posed no danger. Reporters linked it to the upper stage of a rocket.
the_real_story.context_note: The object has been secured and posed no danger. Ars Technica first linked it to the upper stage of a Zhuque-2E rocket.

art_style_hint: A harvested Minnesota cornfield at night with a giant scorched metal dome cracked open like an eggshell and a trail of bent corn leading away from it, in a bold neon graphic-novel style.
